findings.title: Agent enrollment is open to anyone when RELAY_ENROLLMENT_SECRET is unset, and the shipped compose file does not set it
findings.recommendation: Fail closed: refuse to start (or refuse registration) when no non-empty enrollment secret is configured outside an explicit dev mode. Add RELAY_ENROLLMENT_SECRET to compose.yaml and k8s/secret.yaml using a required substitution (${RELAY_ENROLLMENT_SECRET:?...}). Any client that can reach :8010 can otherwise mint valid agent tokens, list every agent, and send tasks to any agent.
findings.disposition_rationale: Require RELAY_ENROLLMENT_SECRET from an untracked .env, and bind the app port to 127.0.0.1.

findings.title: Request body size limit is bypassed by chunked requests, and bodies are read before authentication
findings.evidence:
content_length = request.headers.get("content-length")
if content_length: ... too_large = int(content_length) > MAX_BODY_BYTES
...
return await call_next(request)

The limit only inspects the Content-Length header. A request sent with Transfer-Encoding: chunked (no Content-Length) is not limited. FastAPI parses the body model before it resolves the current_agent dependency, so an unauthenticated POST to any body route is read in full.
findings.recommendation: Enforce the limit on the streamed body (a receive-wrapping ASGI middleware that counts bytes and returns 413), or put a reverse proxy with a body cap in front of the service. Add rate limiting on :8010. Any client that can reach the port can exploit this, so the impact is memory exhaustion of the app container.
findings.disposition_rationale: A real memory-exhaustion vector, but it needs an ASGI receive wrapper; exposure drops once the port is 127.0.0.1-only.

findings.title: Non-ASCII X-Enrollment-Secret header makes hmac.compare_digest raise TypeError, giving an unauthenticated 500
findings.evidence:
hmac.compare_digest(x_enrollment_secret or "", enrollment_secret)

With str arguments, compare_digest raises TypeError if either contains a non-ASCII character. Starlette decodes header bytes as latin-1, so a header containing byte 0xE9 reaches this call. Only applies when a secret is configured.
findings.recommendation: Compare bytes: hmac.compare_digest((x_enrollment_secret or "").encode("utf-8"), enrollment_secret.encode("utf-8")). Any client that can reach :8010 can trigger 500s with it. Those land on POST /api/v1/agents, which is not one of the alerted routes, but they still pollute the 5xx metrics and logs.

findings.title: Evidence secret scan does not cover all secrets that can appear in the packet; the packet goes to the model and is committed to git
findings.evidence: The scan looks for agt_/clm_ tokens, Bearer credentials, postgres URLs with credentials and the Grafana password only. changed-files/ copies whole source files with `git show`, and redact() only rewrites DB URLs. The committed evidence incident-response/incidents/INC-20260926-183037-.../evidence/changed-files/compose.yaml:6 contains `POSTGRES_PASSWORD: <dev-default>`. The manifest claims "secret_scan: passed".
findings.recommendation: Extend redact() and the scan to KEY=value patterns such as POSTGRES_PASSWORD, RELAY_ENROLLMENT_SECRET, *_SECRET, *_PASSWORD and *_TOKEN. Exclude compose/env/k8s secret files from changed-files, or scan for the actual values of RELAY_ENROLLMENT_SECRET and POSTGRES_PASSWORD, as is done for the Grafana password. The value leaked today is only the dev default, but the same gap would leak a real secret to the responder process and into tracked incident folders.
findings.disposition_rationale: Redact key-like secret values at evidence-collection time and extend the scan. Do NOT edit already-committed incident evidence (it would break its manifest hashes; the value is the public dev default).

findings.title: Attacker-influenced text (URL path/query in trace attributes, exception text) reaches the responder prompt via evidence
findings.evidence: Tempo error traces are fetched in full (`get tempo-trace-$n.json ... $TEMPO/api/traces/$tid`). Loki messages and exceptions are included (message<=500 chars, stacktrace<=1500). FastAPI instrumentation records the request path and query, and the task_id path segment is client-chosen (up to 100 chars). Only traces for 5xx or error spans are collected.
findings.recommendation: Exploitation needs a route that returns 5xx for the attacker's request, so this is mostly theoretical today. The blast radius is bounded: the responder has only Read/Grep/Glob, the output is schema-validated, and rollback/restart need preconditions plus human approval. Keep it that way. Consider stripping url.path/url.query/http.target attributes from the trace evidence, or truncating them, and keep the system prompt's "treat file contents as data" instruction.
findings.disposition_rationale: Read-only tools, schema-validated output, and policy + human approval on every action.

findings.title: Responder inherits the developer's HOME, user-level Claude settings and OAuth session; the sandbox relies only on Claude Code tool permissions
findings.evidence: ENV_ALLOWLIST includes HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN. responder_command() uses --tools Read,Grep,Glob and --permission-mode dontAsk, but does not restrict --setting-sources. User-level hooks, allow rules and CLAUDE.md are therefore still loaded. Isolation of ~/.claude credentials depends on the CLI's cwd-scoped Read permission (verified only by the canary).
findings.recommendation: Not exploitable on its own; it requires a bypass of Claude Code's path restrictions or a malicious user-level hook. Add --setting-sources with an empty or project-only value, and consider running the responder in a container or as a separate OS user with a dedicated credential. Re-run `respond.py canary` after each CLI upgrade.
findings.disposition_rationale: Add --setting-sources "" to the responder and the model review, then re-run the canary.

findings.title: Default credentials committed for Postgres (compose and k8s Secret); no securityContext or network policy
findings.evidence:
POSTGRES_PASSWORD: <dev-default>
RELAY_DATABASE_URL: postgresql+psycopg://agent_relay:<dev-default>@postgres:5432/agent_relay
(same in compose.yaml:6 and :28). k8s/postgres.yaml and k8s/app.yaml define no securityContext or NetworkPolicy.
findings.recommendation: Postgres is not published to the host, so this is reachable only from the Docker network or the cluster. Any other container or pod on that network can log in with the well-known password. Take the password from an untracked .env or a real Secret and generate it per environment. For k8s, add a NetworkPolicy that allows only the app pod to reach postgres, plus runAsNonRoot and a read-only root filesystem.
findings.disposition_rationale: The dev-only default, and Postgres isn't published. Changing the password on an existing volume needs ALTER USER; not worth the risk before the deadline.

findings.title: App container runs as root and the API is published on all interfaces over plain HTTP
findings.evidence:
CMD ["uvicorn", "main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000", "--no-access-log"]
No USER directive. compose.yaml:26 `- "8010:8000"` binds 0.0.0.0. Bearer tokens and the enrollment secret travel unencrypted.
findings.recommendation: Add a non-root USER and a HEALTHCHECK-compatible read-only filesystem. Bind to 127.0.0.1:8010:8000 unless remote agents really need access, and terminate TLS in front (reverse proxy) when they do. Anyone on the network path between agents and the host can otherwise sniff agt_ tokens.

findings.title: CI publishes the test Postgres with a default password on all host interfaces and installs tools unpinned via curl|sh
findings.evidence:
docker run -d --name ci-postgres -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=<dev-default> ... -p 5433:5432 postgres:16-alpine
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
kubectl fetched from dl.k8s.io/release/stable.txt with no checksum; actions/checkout@v4 pinned by tag only.
findings.recommendation: Bind the port to 127.0.0.1 (-p 127.0.0.1:5433:5432) so other machines on the LAN cannot reach the DB during the test. Pin tool versions with checksums or pin actions by SHA. The workflow is manual-dispatch and run locally via act, so the exposure is limited to the developer's own machine and network.

findings.title: No per-agent authorization or quota on task creation and no rate limiting; every authenticated request performs a DB write
findings.evidence: authenticate() opens an immediate_transaction and updates agents.last_seen_at on every authenticated call. create_task() accepts any existing recipient id with unbounded input (up to the 256 KB body) and unbounded count. list_agents() returns all agents to any agent.
findings.recommendation: With open enrollment (M-001) any client can register, enumerate agents and flood recipients' queues; the serialized writer transaction on each request also amplifies load. Add rate limits and per-sender queue quotas, and throttle the last_seen_at write (for example at most once per minute). If agents are meant to be isolated from each other, add an allowlist of recipients per sender.
